This is the plainest example in the plugin of a CV input that takes the knob over rather than adding to it. Tangle::process computes gain = CV * knob / range when the Level CV jack is patched, and gain = knob when it is not. A patched cable resting at 0V silences the channel however far up the knob is, and the knob becomes an attenuator for the CV.

The four channels are written from the same shape of code and differ only in which port and which knob they use, so one line covers each role and the tags point all four at it.

The Mix jack is a normalled sum: each channel output's channel count is read and that channel drops out of the total when it is patched. The maker's own product page for the hardware describes the same behaviour.

The level knobs are configured 0 to 1 with a default of 1 and a display multiplier of 100, so they are percentages and come up fully open. The lights are fed the gain value, not the audio.

The menu is named "Voltage Range", with the two choices 10V and 5V. The stored range is compared against 5, and 10 is stored for index 0 and 5 for index 1, so 10V is the first choice and the one a new module has.
